spec.title: Parallel work within an existing campaign

scope.title: 1. Increase useful concurrency without replacing the plan

p.PARALLEL-SCOPE: Use parallelism to finish accepted outcomes sooner under the current owner instruction. Keep the complete schema-1 plan, task ids, dependencies, acceptance obligations and existing campaign fields. A parallel frontier is a derived view, not another queue, execution authority, dependency editor or product scheduler. Planning-only instructions and execution holds still apply.

p.TWO-WORK-SHAPES: The coordinator may dispatch independent existing tasks whose declared prerequisites are accepted, or divide one ready task into bounded disjoint worker packets under that task's existing id. In the second case, the union must establish the entire parent obligation before its acceptance advances. Packet labels are temporary work identities, not new plan nodes or a way to accept a partial parent. Do not remove or bypass a dependency merely because the next task looks parallelizable.

p.PREPARATION-BOUNDARY: Read-only inventory, test design or review can accompany production when each has a separate useful question and named available inputs. Preparation for later work does not start its blocked implementation, treat a proposed interface as accepted, or satisfy its prerequisites. A reviewer may inspect a candidate as a candidate; dependent implementation waits for its required acceptance tier. Return missing inputs as preparation findings rather than filling them with assumptions.

p.SHARED-CONTRACT: Before related workers start, capture the governing accepted contract and relevant source snapshot, prerequisite artifacts and exact task obligations. Settle shared interfaces centrally first. A shared base commit alone is insufficient when dirty files, generated inputs or external configuration affect that contract. Workers report any input drift or missing rule before relying on it.

p.PARALLEL-PACKET: A packet names the existing task id and role; the relevant standing files and permanent anchors; accepted inputs and their identities; exact read and write perimeters; shared resources and their owner; selected checks and expected cases; artifact/report location and recoverable job identity when available; integration owner and safe stop. State what the coordinator will integrate. Keep the packet bounded: workers load the named instructions, not the whole boot lane, personal context or campaign. Missing context is a packet defect.

p.OUTER-PERIMETER: Narrow worker paths within the existing task's authorized outer perimeter. Broad task directories are not evidence of disjointness. Needed shared registration, manifest, schema or generated-output changes must have an authorized owner; a worker cannot silently widen its packet to include them. If the outer task omitted a necessary path, reconcile that bounded scope defect under the existing authority before dispatch. A supplied binding describes a perimeter; it does not grant access.

p.READ-WRITE-CONFLICTS: Check both write/write overlap and a writer changing another worker's read subject. Include directory ancestry, actual path aliases, generated inputs, configuration and semantic interface dependencies. Disjoint filenames alone do not prove independence. Use a captured immutable input, isolate and later reconcile, or serialize the conflicting work. Unknown paths, patterns, external roots or input closure need binding; never interpret unknown as conflict-free. Refresh these judgments when the input or actual diff changes.

p.INTEGRATION-OWNER: Name one integration owner for shared registration files, manifests, schemas, generators and their outputs. Workers may return separate proposals for that owner; they do not race to edit the common file. Set integration order before applying those proposals. An isolated worktree can retain overlapping candidate changes safely but does not prove their semantic independence or make them accepted. Reconcile each candidate on the resulting acceptance tree.

pipeline.title: 3. Match production to review and machine capacity

p.PIPELINE-SUBJECTS: Production of one independent task, preparation or precheck of another stable candidate, and central acceptance of a third may overlap. Freeze or identify each inspected subject so a reviewer does not unknowingly judge changing bytes. Worker review is evidence for the coordinator, never delegated acceptance authority. Choose additional independent review when its question and expected value justify it; do not require a producer/reviewer/tester trio for every small edit.

p.REVIEW-CAPACITY: Size the active work window by observed production, review and integration capacity. When viable unjudged candidates accumulate faster than the coordinator can process them, prioritize judgment and stop adding producers until the backlog is manageable. Prefer work that removes the actual bottleneck; agent count and simultaneous activity are not outcome measures. No universal worker count is imposed.

p.HEAVY-RESOURCES: Worker concurrency and expensive command concurrency are separate decisions. Name the build directory, Docker daemon or namespace, port, database, generator output or other shared resource relevant to each command, with an owner and compatible access mode. Account for observed memory, CPU, disk and provider capacity. Serialize contending heavy commands when parallel execution only duplicates work, blocks on a tool lock or harms throughput. Metadata is not a live resource reservation; check actual jobs and resource use before starting. Unknown capacity is a reason to bind or measure narrowly, not to invent a global quota.

p.PARALLEL-VERIFICATION: Apply `verification-selection.xml` to every packet: select affected build targets and cases before execution, retain compatible build artifacts, and avoid a cold target directory or full suite per worker. Share build caches only where the toolchain and concurrent access are compatible. An artifact cache is not a passing test. One stable integrated run may serve several obligations with a separate claim-to-result mapping for each; never defer a prerequisite gate until after its dependent action. Mutations remain suspicion-triggered and their episode budget is shared across workers and retries for the same subject.

analysis.title: 4. A read-only frontier, never a dispatcher

p.FRONTIER-HELPER: The optional `steward-parallel` skill runs `scripts/parallel_frontier.py` against a complete existing plan and its task descriptions. The helper emits schema-1 JSON with `ready`, `active`, `review_queue`, `blocked`, `conflicts` and `proposed_batches`. It checks declared dependencies and reports known path/resource intersections and missing bindings. Suppressing ancestor states keep descendants out of new dispatch proposals; recorded active jobs and candidates remain visible for reconciliation. It never writes plans or repositories, launches jobs, accepts work or grants authority; `dispatch_authorized` is always `false` and `policy_state` is `requires-binding`.

p.FRONTIER-BINDINGS: Optional JSON bindings carry schema 1, the plan id, revision and SHA-256 of the exact raw TOML, plus per-task exact read/write paths and resource ids/access modes. They are a local, disposable explanation of the analysis inputs, not an accepted plan, shared index, live lock or persisted global worker queue. Bindings must narrow the existing task metadata and refer to that exact plan snapshot. The initial helper accepts repository-contained paths; an external documentation repository requires its own explicit binding and coordination outside that path model. Do not disguise external input as a guessed local path.

p.FRONTIER-LIMITS: Even with exact perimeters, the coordinator still verifies current source identities, surviving jobs, actual resource capacity, semantic independence and current authority. The helper's candidate batches are inspection suggestions, not launch recipes or proof that other writers are absent. Resolve missing bindings within current authority; this read-only check creates no additional owner approval ritual. Use it when choosing a parallel window or diagnosing review contention, not as a compulsory ceremony before every atom.

p.PARALLEL-RECOVERY: If the coordinator loses quota or disappears, workers may finish only their existing bounded packets and then stop at the declared boundary. They do not expand the window, launch replacement jobs or claim acceptance. A resumed coordinator discovers live jobs, retained candidate artifacts and consumed retry episodes before dispatching replacements. Resolve unknown effects before replay and stop or isolate an old writer before starting a conflicting replacement, under `interruption-recovery.xml`. Missing narration is not worker failure.

p.DOCUMENTATION-INPUT: Documentation being prepared elsewhere remains an unavailable input until its source and ownership are supplied. Do not guess paths, treat another worker's changing tree as frozen, or overwrite its files. Once supplied, capture its repository or source root, version or content identity, active writer and write ownership, build commands, and source-to-generated-output mapping. Update only affected packets, topic mappings and proof selections. Initial inventory or reference checks may run in parallel within an authorized ready task on that captured input; existing documentation dependencies and final reconciliation gates remain in force.

p.NARROW-RECONCILIATION: An incoming documentation revision or integrated code change invalidates the results whose relevant inputs moved. Rebind those inputs, refresh affected topic/claim mappings and rerun the necessary checks. Keep unchanged accepted evidence and the complete campaign route. Adaptation of packets and derived views does not require reauthoring all tasks; an actual conflict in mandate or architecture is resolved explicitly rather than hidden by parallel execution.
